items.title: 3-2-1: On building a reserve of resilience, making habits easy, and the value of enthusiasm
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Train while it’s easy so you’re ready when it’s hard.”

​II.

“Unshared knowledge is like potential energy. It’s nice to have, but it only moves things when you transform it into something else. Your contribution is what you share, not what you know.”

III.

“Spend less time trying to find motivation and more time making good habits the path of least resistance.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Novelist and writer Louisa May Alcott reminds us that enthusiasm is a real asset in any endeavor:

“She brought so much love, energy, and cheerfulness to the work that she could not but succeed.”

Source: Little Women

​II.

Author Leo Tolstoy encourages us to walk deliberately toward a grand vision by focusing on our daily output:

“… for a man walking a thousand miles it is absolutely necessary to set aside his final goal and to say to himself each morning: ‘Today I will walk twenty-five miles to a resting place and sleep,’ and during each day’s journey reaching that resting place eclipses his ultimate goal and becomes his sole focus.”

Source: War and Peace (edited lightly for clarity)

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Can my current habits carry me to my desired future?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​Ah, my best party trick​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On being proactive, learning to cook, and optimizing for impact over fame
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Overnight success always takes a year or two.”

​II.

“Speed is rewarded in life.

  • Decisive. Make decisions quickly and you can correct them faster.
  • Proactive. Solve problems now, while they are still small.
  • Bold. Go for it today rather than delaying your dreams.

Don’t rush, but don’t wait.”

III.

“Long-term thinking changes your short-term actions.

  • When you intend to invest long-term, it changes which stocks you buy.
  • When you intend to be in a relationship long-term, it changes the type of person you look for.
  • When you intend to stay injury-free for the long term, it changes the type of workouts you do.

Build what lasts.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Chef and television personality Julia Child on learning to cook (or learning anything):

“The only real stumbling block is fear of failure. In cooking you’ve got to have a what-the-hell attitude.”

She also said, “To be a good cook you have to have a love of the good, a love of hard work, and a love of creating.”

Source: Particular Passions

​II.

George Eliot reminds us that we should not worry about making the history books, but rather on making the world better:

“… for the growing good of the world is partly dependent on unhistoric acts; and that things are not so terrible for you and me as they might have been, is half owing to the number who lived faithfully a hidden life and rest in unvisited tombs.”

Source: Middlemarch

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

You’re always learning, even when you’re not intending to learn. Based on how you are spending your time this week, what are you learning?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​Curry up and get something to eat​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On refusing to give up, the refrains of nature, and making things fun
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“The sooner you make a choice, the sooner you can make an adjustment.”

​II.

“Are you willing to be uncomfortable for 5 minutes?

Exercising is easier once you’ve started the workout. Conversation is easier once you’re already talking. Writing is easier once you’re in the middle of it.

But many rewards in life will elude you if you’re not willing to be a little uncomfortable at first.”

III.

“Success is wanting to be where you are.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Marine biologist Rachel Carson on resilience and the rhythm of healing:

“Those who contemplate the beauty of the earth find reserves of strength that will endure as long as life lasts. There is something infinitely healing in the repeated refrains of nature — the assurance that dawn comes after night, and spring after winter.”

Source: The Sense of Wonder

​II.

Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius on refusing to give up:

“Until death, all defeat is psychological.”

Source: It’s unlikely Aurelius wrote this exact phrase. He covers similar themes in Meditations, but there is no source material with this specific wording. Still, I like this one too much to not include it.

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

A question I first heard from ​Greg Isenberg​ and have returned to many times:

What would this look like if it was fun?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​Day 1 vs. Day 2​
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: How to feel good again, choosing your information diet, and the secret to connecting with people
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Your mind will follow whatever you feed it.

Want better thoughts? Consume better things.”

​II.

“It only takes five minutes to break the cycle.

Five minutes of exercise and you are back on the path. Five minutes of writing and the manuscript is moving forward again. Five minutes of conversation and the relationship is restored.

It doesn’t take much to feel good again.”

III.

“It’s remarkable how often the real problem is not what happened, but how it was communicated.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Austrian physicist Lise Meitner, co-discoverer of nuclear fission and a survivor of World War I and World War II, on living well:

“I always arrived at the conclusion that life need not be easy provided only that it is not empty.”

Source: Looking Back

​II.

Jesuit priest Anthony de Mello on how to deliver a message that will connect with people:

“The shortest distance between a human being and Truth is a story.”

Source: One Minute Wisdom

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Energy seems to magically appear when there is genuine interest.
What are you excited to learn?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​I’ll be using these in my next meeting​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On staying in the game, the power of best practices, and how to handle bad events
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“If you spend too much time thinking about the past, you miss out on what you have right now.

Reflecting, learning, and moving on is a fruitful cycle. But replaying old mistakes and revisiting past injustices is a fast way to lose the opportunity of today.

Don’t let one bad event beat you twice.”

​II.

“In the long run, the opportunities that are right for you have a way of finding you. Sometimes you wish so dearly that a new relationship or a big chance will go your way. It can feel like heartbreak when it falls through. But you have to dust yourself off and keep reaching and keep working. Water always finds its level. Stay in the game, keep your energy high, and do your best each day. You’ll find the moments that are meant for you.”

III.

“Collect ideas on all the best practices in your industry and use that list as your starting point. Then, combine, iterate, and distill the list into what works best for your situation and plays to your strengths. Let the best material be your starting material. Then, make it your own.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Novelist and short story writer Henry Miller encourages us to spend more time appreciating and less time ruminating:

“Develop interest in life as you see it; in people, things, literature, music — the world is so rich, simply throbbing with rich treasures, beautiful souls and interesting people. Forget yourself.”

Source: ​Henry Miller Memorial Library​

​II.

Philosopher and writer Friedrich Engels reminds us that small actions beat big thoughts:

“An ounce of action is worth a ton of theory.”

Source: This quote is unconfirmed and has probably been modified over the years. Engels wrote in German and the more common phrasing translates to something like, “Every step of real movement is more important than a dozen programs.”

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

What are my favorite hours of the day and what adjustments can I make to ensure they are under my control?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​This is never a good thing​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On spotting new opportunities, the power of high volume, and how to make a big decision
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Mental toughness immediately increases when you find the right subject. You’re more likely to stick with things when you’re genuinely interested.”

​II.

“How to see opportunities others miss:

1) Study a totally different field, then return to the original problem. Apply insights from other domains.

2) Invert the problem. Try to achieve the opposite.

3) Find ways to engage with hyper-creative people. Their thinking will rub off.”

III.

“The person who gets 1 shot needs everything to go right.

The person who gets 1000 shots is going to score at some point.

Find a way to play the game that ensures you get a lot of shots.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Journalist and author Hunter S. Thompson on going for it:

“Who is the happier man, he who has braved the storm of life and lived, or he who has stayed securely on shore and merely existed?”

Source: Security (1955)

​II.

Science fiction writer Ursula K. Le Guin on the process:

“It is good to have an end to journey towards; but it is the journey that matters, in the end.”

Source: The Left Hand of Darkness

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Here’s one from the writer, ​Isabel Unraveled​:

“A good heuristic when making a big decision: would choosing this make me feel more alive?”

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​Never doubt your greatness​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: How to start a new habit, the power of responsibility, and prioritizing the long-term
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“When choosing a new habit many people seem to ask themselves, “What can I do on my best days?”

The trick is to ask, “What can I stick to even on my worst days?”

Start small. Master the art of showing up. Scale up when you have the time, energy, and interest.”

​II.

“Concentration produces wealth.

Diversification protects wealth.”

III.

“Life rarely changes in a positive way without an increase in responsibility.

This is true in many areas: taking ownership of your health, committing to a relationship, starting a business, etc.

Whatever it is, if you want the trajectory to change, the amount of responsibility usually has to change.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Writer Haruki Murakami on time and money:

“Spend your money on the things money can buy. Spend your time on the things money can’t buy.”

Source: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle

​II.

Farmer, novelist, and poet, Wendell Berry, on thinking long-term and acting in the long-term good:

“Invest in the millennium. Plant sequoias. Say that your main crop is the forest that you did not plant, that you will not live to harvest.”

Source: ​Manifesto: The Mad Farmer Liberation Front

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

If not now, when?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​An underrated moment in human history​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: What to do when you feel stuck, the art of following up, and how to build something successful
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“We are all connected. The way you choose to live ripples into the future. Your decisions today can be a blessing or a curse for your descendants. Strive to live in such a way that the world will gain from your time here.”

II.

“Winning isn’t what makes you feel good. Growth makes you feel good.

Sometimes they are the same thing. When you achieve something for the first time, it’s growth. You’ve reached a new level. The win feels satisfying. But when you do it for the tenth time (or the hundredth time), it can feel stale. You’re still winning, but you’re not necessarily growing.

The secret is not to worry about winning, but rather to focus on growing. And the most straightforward way to grow is to learn something. If you’re ever feeling stuck, go learn something new. Read, write, think, learn, repeat.

When you’re learning, you’re growing.”

III.

“The person who complains loudest will get attention, but at the expense of their reputation.

And yet, following up is an important life skill. If you want something done and you’d like it done soon, then you need to follow up.

The balance is in the delivery. Be pleasant and persistent when things matter to you. Always kind, but don’t let it rest until it’s done and done well.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Martin Lorentzon, cofounder of Spotify, reminds us that the way to build a successful company (and, in many ways, a successful life) is to focus on being useful:

“The value of a company is the sum of all problems solved.”

Source: ​David Senra, Interview with Daniel Ek​

II.

French military commander and statesman, Napoleon Bonaparte, on reading each situation accurately and working with it:

“I had few really definite ideas, and the reason for this was that, instead of obstinately seeking to control circumstances, I obeyed them, and they forced me to change my mind all the time. Thus it happened that most of the time, to tell the truth, I had no definite plans but only projects.”

Source: A conversation in 1816 as quoted in The Mind of Napoleon. Elsewhere, Napoleon was quoted as saying that people rise “by their adaptability to circumstances.”

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Spend less time dreaming and more time experimenting.

Doing the real thing will usually teach you more than dreaming about the perfect thing. What is one small way you can try out the real thing (even if only for five minutes or at a smaller scale)?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​My morning routine​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On starting over, how to train and how to compete, and the magic of consistency
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Opportunities shrink or expand in proportion to your enthusiasm.”

​II.

“You can’t start last week, but you can start now. Stop dwelling on what you should have done or ruminating on the mistakes you made. Channel that energy into the next good choice. You have today and you can try again.”

III.

“Modern life is largely spent in three positions: sitting, standing, and lying down.

Try to break the mold. Spend more time this week doing something besides sitting, standing, or lying down. Go for a walk, stretch in the grass, swim in the pool, kneel in the garden, climb a hill. Or you can sit or stand, but add something to it. Paint while you stand. Bike while you sit.

Our physical abilities rarely vanish overnight. They usually fade away from disuse. The body trains for tomorrow based on what it is asked to do today.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Freestyle skier and model Eileen Gu, winner of three Olympic gold medals, on the different mindsets needed for training and competition:

“I train like I’ve never won, and I compete like I’ve never lost.”

Source: ​On Purpose​

​II.

Writer and illustrator Tim Urban on consistency:

“Something I try to remind myself: someone who is writing three hours a day, five days a week… it’s shocking how much you can produce. Add those weeks together, and 40 weeks later, you have a book.

The difference between the prolific writer and the self-loathing person who doesn’t write anything is one writes 15 hours a week out of their 112 waking hours a week and the other does zero out of 112 waking hours. So 1/7th versus 0/7ths.

6/7ths of those two people’s lives are the same! People who can’t put something together have this daunting assumption that the prolific writer is fundamentally different, they’re working constantly all the time. It doesn’t have to be that way. It’s consistency.”

Source: ​The Tim Ferriss Show​

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Rather than thinking about what you want to accomplish or obtain this week, let’s spin it around.

What can you accept or let go of this week?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​How I’m going to start signing my emails​…
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On thinking long-term, how to attract like-minded people, and one sign of mental toughness
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Long-term thinking changes short-term actions. Spend a little time today doing things that will benefit you in ten years.”

​II.

“One sign of mental toughness is being larger than the situation.

Do the circumstances dictate your mood and emotions? Or do you choose your mood and emotions, and the situation is simply something you respond to?

The less your mood depends on your circumstances, the more mentally tough you are.”

III.

“There is no path to greatness without hard work. And the only person who feels like working hard for years is someone who is excited about the task.

You only get one life and you’re going to burn the days either way, so the real question is: What excites you and interests you? What makes you feel curious and alive, perhaps even joyful? What is so “worth it” that you’re not worried about the tradeoffs, the hard work, the hassle?

Follow your enthusiasm.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Country music star and philanthropist Dolly Parton on making things better:

“I was born with a happy heart. I’ve always tried to let that shine even during my dark times. I’m one of those people who, even if things are not right, goes about trying to make it as right as I can rather than just lying around on my ass and wallowing in it all day. I think, “Well, I can either do this or I can do that.” I choose to get up and try to make it better if I can…

Of course, I try to improve every day. If there’s a better outfit, I want to wear it. If there’s a better song, I want to write it. If there’s a better record, I want to record it. If there’s a better movie, I want to make it. I will continue to be as good as I can be. And I intend to keep coming up with new ideas all the time.”

Source: Behind the Seams: My Life in Rhinestones

​II.

The psychiatrist Carl Jung reminds us that great work is a magnet for like-minded people:

“No matter how isolated you are and how lonely you feel, if you do your work truly and conscientiously, unknown friends will come and seek you.”

Source: Letter to Miguel Serrano (September 14, 1960)

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Pick one room where you spend a lot of time. What is one item in this room that you no longer use or do not benefit from?

Keep what serves you or inspires you. Remove what distracts you.

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​The guy who cuts you off in traffic​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: What good judgement requires, how to direct your attention, and the hidden path to happiness
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“The measure of a life is not what you consume, but what you contribute.

Spend less time owning, consuming, taking. Spend more time giving, creating, making.”

​II.

“Everyone wants to be happy now, but it might be better to optimize for being satisfied later.

Perhaps the key to happiness is to not worry about being happy today, but rather to make choices that will leave your future self feeling satisfied with how you chose to live. Do you feel a sense of satisfaction with the choices you made? With the way you lived today? With the things you chose to focus on over the last year? Are you “happy” with the impact you are making?

Momentary happiness is hard to predict, but deep satisfaction is easier to control. It is on the other side of good choices, good habits, and meaningful impact.”

III.

“Your life is simply your days, accumulated. Did today’s habits contribute to the life you want to build?”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Neurobiologist and Nobel Prize winner Rita Levi-Montalcini reminds us that good judgment requires warmth and logic:

“Rare are those people who use the mind; few use the heart; and really unique are those who use both.”

Source: WIRED Interview (March 2009)

​II.

Author and speaker Jim Rohn reminds us to continually redirect our attention toward what is helpful and productive:

“Much of life is in learning to always remain part of the solution rather than allowing ourselves to become part of the problem.”

Source: The Seasons of Life

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

If the version of you from five years ago could see your life today, what would surprise them most?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​I want this dog​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On the power of curiosity, winning vs. improving, and taking control of your to-do list
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Being curious and excited can take you far, especially over the long arc of a life. The person who is a voracious lifelong learner will figure it out eventually. A strong reader with a healthy dose of curiosity and a willingness to try things is hard to stop.”

II.

“Delaying a conversation doesn’t make it easier.”

III.

“Who is initiating the items on your to-do list?

When I’m most productive, I decide what I want to create and work on the task that will help build my vision.

When I am less productive, I spend my day responding to what someone else sends to me — emails, texts, etc. — and often that means I end up building someone else’s vision.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Modernist painter Georgia O’Keeffe on making your vision a reality:

“Whether you succeed or not is irrelevant — there is no such thing. Making your unknown known is the important thing.”

Source: Georgia O’Keeffe: Art and Letters

II.

Professor and writer Joseph Campbell on following your passion:

“If you do follow your bliss, you put yourself on a kind of track that has been there all the while, waiting for you, and the life that you ought to be living is the one you are living. When you can see that, you begin to meet people who are in your field of bliss, and they open doors to you. I say: follow your bliss and don’t be afraid, and doors will open where you didn’t know they were going to be.”

Source: Joseph Campbell and the Power of Myth with Bill Moyers

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Focus less on winning, focus more on improving. What can you do today to feel like you are growing?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​Brent always took it a little too far​…
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On living with lightness, emphasizing what works, and the simple way to gain clarity
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Clarity isn’t about knowing what you want to do with your life, it’s about knowing what you want to do this week. You don’t need to have it all figured out. You just need to know your next step.”

​II.

“When you’re on a good path: It’s only a failure if you stop. It’s a lesson if you keep going.

When you’re on a bad path: It’s only a failure if you keep going. It’s a lesson if you stop.”

III.

“You can’t get lucky if you don’t take action. The best opportunity in the world is just a missed opportunity if you don’t grab it.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Journalist Doris Veillette reminds us to receive the day with positive energy and we will be positioned to make the most of it:

“Smile to life this morning and be assured, ma’am, that this life will make you smile. The present belongs to the optimists.”

Source: Forbidden to Men

​II.

George Leonard, a writer, editor, and fifth-degree black belt in aikido, encourages us to live with lightness:

“Without laughter, the rough and rocky places on the path might be too painful to bear. Humor not only lightens your load, it also broadens your perspective. To be deadly serious is to suffer tunnel vision. To be able to laugh at yourself clears the vision.”

Source: Mastery

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Try this simple reframe from executive coach, ​Joe Hudson​:

Instead of thinking, “What’s wrong and how do I fix it?”

Try exploring, “What’s right and how do I grow it?”

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​Excuse me, would you like to solve a murder​?
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On the magic of wanting less, changing inch by inch, and building a sense of hope
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“If you always want more, then you’ll find the most you can have will always be too little.”

​II.

“Large, sweeping changes often sound good in theory, but the faster you try to change your life, the more likely you are to backslide. Real change is inch by inch. Go out and win the next five minutes.”

III.

“Whatever can be measured grabs our attention. How much money we make. How much weight we can lift. How many bedrooms are in the house.

And once we notice a number, it is natural to want to improve it. We find ourselves wondering how to make more money, lift more weight, add another bedroom. What is measurable becomes what is important. Not because it matters more, but because it is easier to see.

Sometimes a new perspective is helpful. Rather than asking, “How can I get more?” Try asking, “What is an inspiring way to live?”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

The 4th Earl of Chesterfield, Philip Dormer Stanhope, on focus:

“There is time enough for everything, in the course of the day, if you do but one thing at once; but there is not time enough in the year, if you will do two things at a time.”

Source: Letter to his son. Letter IX (April 14, 1747).

​II.

Investor Charlie Munger on hardship and perseverance:

“Assume life will be really tough, and then ask if you can handle it. If the answer is yes, you’ve won.”

“Life is very likely to provide terrible blows, unfair blows. Some people recover, and others don’t. And there I think the attitude of Epictetus helps guide one to the right reaction. He thought that every mischance in life, however bad, created an opportunity to behave well. He believed every mischance provided an opportunity to learn something useful. And one’s duty was not to become immersed in self-pity, but to utilize each terrible blow in a constructive fashion.”

Source: The first quote is unsourced. The second is from the USC Gould School of Law Commencement Address (May 13, 2007)

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Greet each morning with a sense of hope.

What grand future are you building?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​No shame in this, Barbara​.
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On leisure vs. luxury, unlocking growth, and the many versions of a good life
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“Achievements are great. It is satisfying to accomplish something. It feels good to win. And many achievements make the world a better place, too.

But also remember to ask, “What am I really trying to accomplish here?” You may realize the goal is not to write a best-selling book or earn that promotion or get into medical school, but rather to build a life you enjoy. And there are many versions of a life you enjoy.

It is often the case that if you can release the narrative of “I have to do this” to be happy, then a different (but equally lovely) life is waiting for you.”

​II.

“Plenty of growth can be found in removing your vices, but the real leaps are unlocked when you stop clinging to your comforts.”

III.

“Whether you have ten years left or a hundred years left, your life is an incredibly brief moment. We know for sure you won’t be here in a century.

But today? Today you are in the Great Game. And this moment you have right now might as well be the most important moment in the universe. Your time is thin. Go out and live fully now.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Inventor and author Lin Yutang on leisure vs. luxury:

“The enjoyment of leisure is something which decidedly costs less than the enjoyment of luxury. All it requires is an artistic temperament which is bent on seeking a perfectly useless afternoon spent in a perfectly useless manner.”

Source: The Importance of Living (1937)

​II.

Novelist Paulo Coelho on resilience:

“I ask myself: are defeats necessary?

Well, necessary or not, they happen. When we first begin fighting for a dream, we have no experience and make mistakes. The secret of life, though, is to fall seven times and to get up eight times.”

Source: The Alchemist

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Challenge yourself to have one new experience this week. When everything around you is familiar, the days turn stale and slip by unnoticed. A surprising experience breathes life into tired days and makes the mind fresh again. What is one new experience you can have this week?

Until next week,

James Clear
Author of ​Atomic Habits​
Cofounder of ​Authors Equity​

p.s. ​Watching Indiana Jones for the first time​…
items.author: James Clear

items.title: 3-2-1: On protecting your mind, the recipe for frustration, and how to spark better conversation
items.content:
3 IDEAS FROM ME

I.

“The recipe for frustration is taking something on that requires a whole person, but only giving it half your time.

Look at what you’re trying to do. What is required? Some things can only be done well when they are pursued with full effort.”

​II.

“It’s hard to learn when you feel defensive.

Relax. You are capable and you can recover from whatever you face.

You can accept feedback without taking it personally. What is this moment teaching you?”

III.

“When you ignore a problem that is small enough to handle, it often grows into a problem too big to manage.”

2 QUOTES FROM OTHERS

I.

Film actress and producer Mary Pickford on protecting your mind:

“All the water in the world cannot sink a ship unless it gets inside the ship. All the negativity in the world cannot sink a person unless it gets inside the mind.”

Source: Why Not Try God (1934)

​II.

French novelist Gustave Flaubert on happiness:

“The secret of being happy consists of knowing how to enjoy yourself—enjoy being at table, in bed, enjoy standing up, sitting down, enjoy the nearest ray of sunshine, the slightest bit of landscape: in other words, love everything.”

Source: His private notebook, Souvenirs, written from 1838–1841.

1 QUESTION FOR YOU

Psychologist and author Adam Grant shares a question for sparking better conversation…

“When you meet someone new, don’t ask: What do you do? It limits what people share about themselves to a job description.

Instead, try: What do you love to do? It ignites curiosity and invites people to express their distinctive interests.”

Until next week,
